newsitem.title: FRANCE: French banks cut base rates after BoF cut.
newsitem.headline: French banks cut base rates after BoF cut.

text.p: Leading French commercial banks said on Friday they were cutting their base rates after the Bank of France trimmed a key official rate on Thursday.
BNP, Societe Generale, Credit Lyonnais and CCF said they were cutting their base rates to 6.55 percent from 6.75 percent effective Monday.
The reduction also follows a fall in market rates.

The base rate is the rate at which banks lend to their best customers but rates to other clients usually follow in the same direction making it generally cheaper for French companies and consumers to borrow money.

The Bank of France on Thursday said it was lowering its intervention rate to 3.25 percent from 3.35 percent, in an apparent sign of approval of the goverment's 1997 austerity budget presented on Wednesday.

Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet said in a television interview on Thursday the rate cut had been made possible by a slowdown in inflation and by a recovery of the franc on the foreign exchanges.
